dv.body:
އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި މިއަދު ރާއްޖެ ވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

އެމަނިކުފާނަށް މާފަރު އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއާޕޯޓުން މަރުޙަބާ ދެންނެވީ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދާއި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ގެ އިސް އޮފިޝަލުންނާއި، ނ. އަތޮޅު ކައުންސިލް ރައީސް އާއި ނ. މާފަރު ކައުންސިލްގެ މެންބަރުންނެވެ.

އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒްގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ ލައިން އޮފް ކްރެޑިޓްގެ އެހީގައި ހިންގާ ހަނިމާދޫ އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއަރޕޯޓް ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓްގެ ޢަމަލީ މަސައްކަތް ފެށުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގަންނަވާނެއެވެ. އަދި މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި، އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގައި ށ.ފޯކައިދޫގައި ޤާއިމް ކުރެވިފައިވާ ށ.ފޯކައިދޫ ކޮމިޔުނިޓީ ސެންޓަރ އިފްތިތާޙް ކުރެއްވުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ބައިވެރިވެ ވަޑައިގަތުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިހުގެ އަރިހަށް އިޚްތިރާމްގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއްކުރެއްވުމާއި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުއާ ބައްދަލު ކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އޭގެ އިތުރުން، ހއ.އުތީމަށް ވަޑައިގަންނަވައި، އުތީމު ގަނޑުވަރަށް އިޙުތިރާމުގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވާ ގޮތަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ.

މިއީ އިންޑިއާގެ އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް މިނިސްޓަރުގެ ހައިޞިއްޔަތުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރައްވާ ހަތަރުވަނަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ. އެންމެފަހުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ރާއްޖެއަށް ވަޑައިގެންފައިވަނީ 2022 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ މާރޗް މަހު އައްޑޫ ސިޓީއަށެވެ.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Nepal
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Nepal
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Nepal

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a congratulatory message to Honourable Dr Bimala Rai Paudyal on her appointment as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Nepal.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"It is with great pleasure that I extend to Your Excellency my heartfelt congratulations on your appointment as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Nepal.

As close friends and partners, the Maldives and Nepal have enjoyed years of strong bilateral collaboration, which has significantly contributed to the growth of our relationship. Let me express my eagerness to collaborate closely with you on bilateral and international levels for the mutual benefit of our two nations and peoples.

With Your Excellency as Foreign Minister, I am confident that the Maldives-Nepal collaboration will usher in a new era of cooperation based on the ideals of friendship, mutual respect, and understanding.

I am looking forward to meeting with you and sharing perspectives on how we can further enhance our bilateral cooperation and friendship.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration."

ENDS

en.title: Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India arrives in Maldives, on an Official Visit
en.description: Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India arrives in Maldives, on an Official Visit
en.body:
Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India arrives in Maldives, on an Official Visit

The Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar arrived on an Official Visit to Maldives this afternoon.

The External Affairs Minister was received at Maafaru International Airport, by the Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, President of the Noonu Atoll Council and members of the Noonu Maafaru Council.

During the visit Minister of External Affairs is scheduled to participate in the groundbreaking ceremony of Hanimaadhoo International Airport Development Project, being constructed under Indian Line of Credit. During the visit, Minister of External Affairs will call on the President of the Maldives Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid.

Both Ministers are scheduled to hold official talks and witness the exchange of several Memorandums of Understanding between the two countries at a ceremony to be held in Noonu Manadhoo. Minister of External Affairs will also participate in the inauguration ceremony of the Shaviyani Foakaidhoo Community Centre. Additionally, during the visit, Minister of External Affairs will visit Haa Alif Utheemu and tour the historical sites.

This is Minister Dr. Jaishankar’s fourth visit to the Maldives, in his capacity as the Minister of External Affairs of India. His last visit was in March 2022 to Addu City.

en.title: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid and Minister of External Affairs, Dr. S. Jaishankar hold official discussions
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid and Minister of External Affairs, Dr. S. Jaishankar hold official discussions
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid and Minister of External Affairs, Dr. S. Jaishankar hold official discussions

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid held bilateral talks with Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar today, at Noonu Manadhoo. Both sides had comprehensive, in-depth, and candid communication during the discussions. They reflected on the historic relationship between both countries and expressed commitment on furthering cooperation in priority areas.

During the official discussion, both Ministers noted the successful economic cooperation and the progress of projects that is being implemented under Indian grant assistance and line of credit schemes. Both Ministers exchanged views and shared their visions relating to development cooperation, tourism cooperation, human resource development, multilateral engagements, and consular affairs between both countries.

Minister Shahid expressed gratitude to the Government of India for the constant support to facilitate and further develop economic, trade and investment ties between both countries, and for India’s commitment in the socioeconomic development of the Maldives.

Minister Dr. Jaishankar is on a two-day official visit to the Maldives, keeping with the renewed tradition of high-level exchanges between the two countries.

en.title: Ceremony held to exchange Memorandums of Understanding between Maldives and India, and handover of two sea ambulances to Ministry of Defense
en.description: Ceremony held to exchange Memorandums of Understanding between Maldives and India, and handover of two sea ambulances to Ministry of Defense
en.body:
Ceremony held to exchange Memorandums of Understanding between Maldives and India, and handover of two sea ambulances to Ministry of Defense

A number of significant Memorandums of Understanding were exchanged between Maldives and India in various fields, expanding the cooperation between two countries at a ceremony held today in Noonu Manadhoo. The ceremony was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, Abdulla Shahid and the Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar.

At today’s ceremony, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel and Indian High Commissioner Munu Mahawar exchanged the Memorandum of Understanding between the Government of Republic of Maldives and Government of India for additional grant assistance of 100 million Rufiyaa for the High Impact Community Development Project scheme. A number of socio-economic development projects are planned to be implemented throughout the country under this funding.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel and Indian High Commissioner Munu Mahawar also exchanged the Memorandum of Understanding for development of a sports complex in Gaafu Dhaal Gadhdhoo. This project will establish a Centre which will promote youth empowerment through sports and contribute to the community development overall.

Additionally, Vice Chancellors of both Maldives National University and Cochin University of Science and Technology exchanged the Memorandum of Understanding on capacity building to facilitate exchanges and co-operative initiative between the two universities in the area of education, research, development instruction, community service, staff and student exchanges.

During the ceremony, both Foreign Minister Shahid and External Affairs Minister Dr. Jaishankar also witnessed the handover of two sea ambulances from the Government of India to the Ministry of Defence of Maldives which was a project carried out under the High Impact Community Development Project Scheme. The symbolic token was received by Deputy Minister of Defence, Uz. Hassan Zameel from the High Commissioner of India, Munu Mahawar. Minister of External Affairs Dr. Jaishankar is on an Official Visit at the invitation of Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid from 18 to 19 January 2023.

en.title: Ambassador of Maldives to Belgium, Omar Abdul Razzak, presents his Letters of Credence to the Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg
en.description: Ambassador of Maldives to Belgium, Omar Abdul Razzak, presents his Letters of Credence to the Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg
en.body:
Ambassador of Maldives to Belgium, Omar Abdul Razzak, presents his Letters of Credence to the Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg

The newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Maldives to the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, Omar Abdul Razzak, presented his Letters of Credence to His Royal Highness the Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg. The ceremony took place at the Grand Ducal Palace in Luxembourg.

The Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg welcomed Ambassador Omar, wishing him success in undertaking his duties. Ambassador Omar thanked The Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg for the audience and conveyed greetings and good wishes from President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives.

During the private audience following the Credential Ceremony, Ambassador Omar assured The Grand Duke Henri of Luxembourg of his commitment to work closely with the Government of Luxembourg to strengthen the close bilateral relations and foster stronger ties between the two countries.

Ambassador Omar was accompanied by his spouse, Aminath Zahir.

dv.title: އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ
dv.description: އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ
dv.body:
އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ

މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު މި މަހުގެ 18 އިން 19 އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ އުތުރުގެ އަތޮޅުތަކަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިހުގެ އަރިހަށް އިޙްތިރާމްގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވާނެއެވެ. އަދި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާ ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގެ އިތުރުން މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ އާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ދެމެދު މުހިންމު އެއްބަސްވުންތަކެއްގައި ސޮއިކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އަދި އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ހަނިމާދޫ އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއަރޕޯޓް ތަރައްޤީ ކުރުމުގެ ޢަމަލީ މަސައްކަތް ފެށުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ބައިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވުމާއި، ށ. ފޯކައިދޫގައި ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ކޮމިއުނިޓީ ސެންޓަރ އިފްތިތާޙް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައިއެވެ. އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ރާއްޖެއަށް މި ކުރައްވާ ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ އެމަނިކުފާނު 2019 ވަނަ އަހަރު މޭ މަހު މަޤާމާ ހަވާލުވިފަހުން ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރައްވާ ހަތަރުވަނަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ. އެންމެ ފަހުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވީ 2022 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ މާރިޗް މަހު އައްޑޫ ސިޓީއަށެވެ.

en.title: Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India to make an Official Visit to the Maldives
en.description: Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India to make an Official Visit to the Maldives
en.body:
Minister of External Affairs of the Republic of India to make an Official Visit to the Maldives

The Minister of External Affairs of India, Dr. S. Jaishankar will make an Official Visit to Northernmost Atolls of Maldives from 18-19 January 2023, on the invitation of the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives Abdulla Shahid.

During the visit, official talks would be held between both Ministers to review the progress on bilateral cooperation, following which several Memorandums of Understanding will be exchanged. The Minister of External Affairs will also call on the President of the Maldives Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

The Minister of External Affairs will also participate in the groundbreaking ceremony of the Hanimaadhoo International Airport Development Project to be undertaken through the Line of Credit arranged by the Government of India and inaugurate the Shaviyani Foakaidhoo Community Centre developed under Indian grant assistance.

Minister Dr. Jaishankar’s last visit to the Maldives was in March 2022 to Addu City. This visit will be Minister Dr. Jaishankar’s fourth visit to the Maldives, since assuming office in May 2019.

dv.description: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު މި މަހުގެ 18 އިން 19 އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ އުތުރުގެ އަތޮޅުތަކަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ…
dv.body:
މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު މި މަހުގެ 18 އިން 19 އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ އުތުރުގެ އަތޮޅުތަކަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިހުގެ އަރިހަށް އިޙްތިރާމްގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވާނެއެވެ. އަދި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާ ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގެ އިތުރުން މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ އާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ދެމެދު މުހިންމު އެއްބަސްވުންތަކެއްގައި

ސޮއިކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އަދި އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ހަނިމާދޫ އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއަރޕޯޓް ތަރައްޤީ ކުރުމުގެ ޢަމަލީ މަސައްކަތް ފެށުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ބައިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވުމާއި، ށ. ފޯކައިދޫގައި ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ކޮމިއުނިޓީ ސެންޓަރ އިފްތިތާޙް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައިއެވެ. އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ރާއްޖެއަށް މި ކުރައްވާ ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ އެމަނިކުފާނު 2019 ވަނަ އަހަރު މޭ މަހު މަޤާމާ ހަވާލުވިފަހުން ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރައްވާ ހަތަރުވަނަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ. އެންމެ ފަހުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވީ 2022 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ މާރިޗް މަހު އައްޑޫ ސިޓީއަށެވެ.

dv.title: އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެ (2)
dv.description: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު މި މަހުގެ 18 އިން 19 އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ އުތުރުގެ އަތޮޅުތަކަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ…
dv.body:
މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޝާހިދުގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ޑރ. އެސް. ޖައިޝަންކަރު މި މަހުގެ 18 އިން 19 އަށް ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އެންމެ އުތުރުގެ އަތޮޅުތަކަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިއްޖެއެވެ. މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އިބްރާހީމް މުޙައްމަދު ޞާލިހުގެ އަރިހަށް އިޙްތިރާމްގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވާނެއެވެ. އަދި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާ ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގެ އިތުރުން މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ އާއި ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ދެމެދު މުހިންމު އެއްބަސްވުންތަކެއްގައި

ސޮއިކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައެވެ. އަދި އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އިންޑިއާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގުމަށް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވާ ހަނިމާދޫ އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއަރޕޯޓް ތަރައްޤީ ކުރުމުގެ ޢަމަލީ މަސައްކަތް ފެށުމުގެ ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ބައިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވުމާއި، ށ. ފޯކައިދޫގައި ޤާއިމުކޮށްފައިވާ ކޮމިއުނިޓީ ސެންޓަރ އިފްތިތާޙް ކުރެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައިއެވެ. އިންޑިއާގެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް އެކްސްޓަރނަލް އެފެއާޒް ރާއްޖެއަށް މި ކުރައްވާ ދަތުރުފުޅަކީ އެމަނިކުފާނު 2019 ވަނަ އަހަރު މޭ މަހު މަޤާމާ ހަވާލުވިފަހުން ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރައްވާ ހަތަރުވަނަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ. އެންމެ ފަހުން އެމަނިކުފާނު ރާއްޖެއަށް ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއް ކުރެއްވީ 2022 ވަނަ އަހަރުގެ މާރިޗް މަހު އައްޑޫ ސިޓީއަށެވެ.

en.title: Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid pays courtesy call on Prime Minister of Cambodia
en.description: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid paid a courtesy call on the Prime Minister of Cambodia, Samdech Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo Hun Sen today
en.body:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid paid a courtesy call on the Prime Minister of Cambodia, Samdech Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo Hun Sen today

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid paid a courtesy call on the Prime Minister of Cambodia, Samdech Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo Hun Sen today, during the Prime Minister’s Official Visit to the Maldives.

At the meeting held at Paradise Island Resort, Minister Shahid welcomed the Prime Minister and his delegation to the Maldives and reaffirmed the view of the Government of Maldives, that both countries can pursue closer cooperation on all aspects of bilateral relations, as well as regionally and internationally.

Minister Shahid further stated that the agreements signed today, will be mutually beneficial to both the people of Maldives and Cambodia and noted that the Visa Exemption Agreement will increase cooperation in the future and will allow greater people-to-people contact. Minister Shahid also noted that the Maldives stands ready to implement the outcomes agreed upon by the two leaders during the Official Talks held in the morning at the President’s Office.   Prime Minister Samdech Akka Moha Sena Padei Techo Hun Sen is currently on an Official Visit to the Maldives from 15 – 17 January 2023 at the invitation of the President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal
en.description: Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends a message of condolence to the Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of condolence to the His Excellency Puspa Kamal Dahal ‘Prachanda’, Prime Minister and Minister for Foreign Affairs of Nepal, following the loss of lives in a tragic airplane crash in the city of Pokhara, Nepal, on 15 January 2023.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

"It was with profound shock and sorrow that I received the news of the plane crash on 15 January 2022 in Pokhara, Nepal causing the tragic loss of lives of those on board.

During this time of distress, the Government and the people of Maldives join me in extending our heartfelt condolences and sympathies to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Nepal.

Please also convey our deepest condolences to the members of the bereaved families.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Permanent Representative of the U.S. to the UN Human Rights Council Calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: The Permanent Representative of the United States (U.S.) to the United Nations Human Rights Council Michèle Taylor, paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign
en.body:
The Permanent Representative of the United States (U.S.) to the United Nations Human Rights Council Michèle Taylor, paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign

The Permanent Representative of the United States (U.S.) to the United Nations Human Rights Council Michèle Taylor, paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, this afternoon. Ambassador Taylor is currently undertaking an official visit to the Maldives from 14 to 17 January 2023, to hold discussions with Government officials and members of the Civil Society.

During the meeting, Minister Shahid and Ambassador Taylor exchanged areas of priority for both countries in the field of human rights, and deliberated further on their respective memberships at the Human Rights Council. In this regard, Minister Shahid outlined the vision set by the Maldives to advance the key areas of its focus at the Council, which include: promotion of gender equality and elimination of violence against women and girls, youth advocacy, climate change and environment, civil society engagement and inclusivity at the Human Rights Council.

Minister Shahid also reaffirmed the Government’s commitment towards the promotion and protection of human rights, as one of the three pillars of its foreign policy. He recognized the U.S. as an important partner of the Maldives in bilateral and multilateral spheres and expressed gratitude towards the assistance provided by the U.S. especially in advancing fundamental rights.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, Joint Secretary Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Joint Secretary Shiuneen Riasheed and Assistant Director Aishath Rayahyn.

en.title: New Ambassador of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, presents Credentials to President Biden
en.description: New Ambassador of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, presents Credentials to President Biden
en.body:
New Ambassador of Maldives, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, presents Credentials to President Biden

The new Ambassador of the Maldives to the United States of America, Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed, presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the United States of America, Joe Biden, today.

Ambassador Ghafoor conveyed to President Biden, the Government, and people of the United States, personal greetings, and sincere best wishes of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. He also reaffirmed the commitment of the Government of Maldives to further consolidate the relations between the two countries. President Biden, in his remarks, congratulated Ambassador Ghafoor and highlighted that Maldives has emerged both as a regional and global leader on climate, democracy, and security. President Biden also applauded Maldives’ efforts to mitigate the impacts of climate change and build resilience.

Ambassador Ghafoor, in his remarks highlighted that Maldives – US relations have endured the test of time over the last five decades. Since the establishment of diplomatic relations in 1965, the partnership between the two countries have continued strengthen its shared values and strong commitment to uphold the fundamental principles of democracy, human rights, and rule of law. The Ambassador also noted that the fundamentals of President Solih’s foreign policy has hinged on fortifying and developing our long-standing ties and increasing engagement with key partners such as the United States. Towards that effort, the re-establishment of a resident mission in the United States, after more than a decade, testifies the growing strength of the relations between the two countries.

The Ambassador also noted on the progress made in the establishment of the very first U.S. Embassy in the Maldives this year. The establishment of these Embassies in the respective capitals of the two countries symbolize the true spirit of friendship that connects the two likeminded countries, despite its geographical distance, said the Ambassador.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid welcomes India’s initiative to champion issues central to the Global South at the Voice of the South Summit
en.description: The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, participated virtually today, in the Voice of the South Summit convened by the Government of India.
en.body:
The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, participated virtually today, in the Voice of the South Summit convened by the Government of India.

The Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, participated virtually today, in the Voice of the South Summit convened by the Government of India.

Speaking at the session entitled “Priorities of the Global South – Ensuring a Conducive Environment”, Foreign Minister Shahid congratulated India on assuming Presidency of the Group of Twenty (G20) and welcomed this initiative by India to give a platform for the Global South to share concerns and discuss solutions to shared challenges.

Foreign Minister Shahid stated that rising levels of public debt, the climate crisis and commodity price fluctuation as some of the key challenges facing countries in the Global South and expressed confidence in India’s Presidency of the G20 to find transformative solutions to these issues. He further thanked India for the development assistance provided to the Maldives throughout the years, noting India’s important role in the recovery efforts and national development of the Maldives. He noted of the opportunity the Summit brings for developing countries, especially non-G20 members, to fight inequality through strengthened and revived South-South partnerships.

The Foreign Ministers session was chaired by Minister of External Affairs of India Dr. S. Jaishankar. Ministers from Armenia, Oman, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Georgia, Iran, Jamaica, Kenya, Panama, Tunisia, and Uganda also participated in the session. India will be the President of G20 from 1 December 2022 until 30 November 2023.

en.title: Maldives assumes membership of the Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025
en.description: Maldives assumes membership of the Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025
en.body:
Maldives assumes membership of the Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025

The Maldives begins its membership of the United Nations Human Rights Council for the term 2023-2025 today. Maldives won a seat on the Human Rights Council following the elections held on 11 October 2022, in New York.

The Maldives membership will be guided by the principles of human rights, democracy and good governance and climate action, which underlies the basic principles of Maldives foreign policy. During the three years of membership, Maldives will strive to advance key areas of human rights in the true spirit of multilateralism. The Maldives membership will contribute towards strengthening of national mechanisms and government institutions at all levels to mainstream and uphold human rights.

The Permanent Representative of the Maldives to the United Nations Offices in Geneva Dr Asim Ahmed, will also serve as the Vice President of the Human Rights Council for 2023 representing the Asia Pacific Group.

The United Nations Human Rights Council is an intergovernmental body within the United Nations System made up of 47 Member States, which are responsible for strengthening the promotion and protection of human rights around the globe.

en.title: New Year Message by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Abdulla Shahid
en.description: New Year Message by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Abdulla Shahid
en.body:
New Year Message by the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives Abdulla Shahid

The year 2022 has been another exceptional year for the Maldives Foreign Service, and for the Maldives internationally, in working towards the realisation of the three pillars of the Maldives foreign policy - human rights, democracy and good governance and climate action.   This year the Ministry of Foreign Affairs marked its 90th anniversary. The Maldives Foreign Service Act entered into effect on 14 May 2022, realising a long-held dream and aspiration of the Maldivian diplomatic service.   This year we continued to raise the Maldivian flag high, reaching all corners of the world. We established diplomatic relations with more countries, totalling to 182 countries. We re-opened the Maldives Embassy in Washington. We welcomed Foreign Ministers of China, Hungary, India, and Türkiye. We joined the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States, and was granted dialogue partner status in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, opening new avenues to enhance our cooperation with the countries of those regions.

Working together with like minded countries, in the Human Rights Council, and the General Assembly, we were successful in declaring access to clean and healthy environment a universal human right.

In our work we prioritised gender equality and building an inclusive and considerate workplace. The Maldives successfully led the establishment of the International Day of Women in Diplomacy to be commemorated on 24 June. We also maintained a high representation of women in the executive committee of the Ministry and gender parity among our Ambassadors. The Ministry also established a family room, upholding its commitment to make a family-friendly, inclusive work environment.   This year, the Maldives completed its Presidency of the United Nations General Assembly.  My “Presidency of Hope” delivered just that – hope. The Presidency navigated through the agenda items of the seventy-sixth session of the General Assembly, while also convening the 11th Emergency Special Session on Ukraine, the resurgence and rebuilding after the COVID-19 pandemic, and also introducing new themes to the General Assembly such as tourism, and the interplay between the various environmental tracks. President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih addressed the General Debate in Dhivehi, while a Maldivian presided over the session - a unique honour.   This year, the Foreign Service continued to work with other countries in enhancing investment, development assistance and easier travel. Since November 2018, our diplomats have facilitated up to $3.4 billion in grants, concessional loans, lines of credits and in kind assistance. We also signed more agreements on visa-free travel. Maldivians can now travel to 86 countries without needing a visa.   The Maldives Foreign Service is now counting towards its centennial year – its 100th anniversary. And the Service remains committed to deliver for the people of the Maldives.   In this coming year 2023, the Ministry will continue to work on realising our core foreign policy principles, enhancing our outreach, deepening our engagement, and making Maldivians proud.   We will continue to engage with all countries, based on mutual respect and mutual benefit, paving the way for more assistance, investment, trade, and easier travel. We will continue to engage with international organisations, firm in our belief in multilateralism, with a view to achieve our national interests and enhance engagement.   We are geared up to facilitate more visitors, and receive high level dignitaries. We anticipate the opening of diplomatic missions of the United States and Australia in the Maldives, further expanding our diplomatic corps.   In the global arena, Maldives will once again assume membership of the Human Rights Council, including serving as the Council’s Vice President. Our priorities on the Council will be around our core foreign policy priorities – human rights, democracy and good governance, and climate action. It will contribute towards strengthening of national mechanisms and government institutions at all levels to mainstream and uphold human rights.   The Maldives will also be campaigning for membership of the United Nations Economic and Social Council for the term 2027-2029, and a non-permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council for the term 2033-2034, furthering our multilateral engagement.   In 2023, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs remains committed to delivering its core mandate, under the guidance of our top diplomat President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih. May this coming year be another successful year for our international engagement, and a prosperous year for our country.

dv.title: ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، އެ ސިޔާސަތާއިގުޅޭ މުހިންމު މައްސަލަތަކާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދައުލަތުގެ އިދާރާތަކާއި، ސްކޫލްދަރިވަރުން ހިމެނޭހެން އަހުލުވެރިކޮށް ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމުގެ ޕްރޮގްރާމްތަކެއް ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓުން 2023 ވަނަ އަހަރު ފެށުމަށް ނިންމައި
dv.description: ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، އެ ސިޔާސަތާއިގުޅޭ މުހިންމު މައްސަލަތަކާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދައުލަތުގެ އިދާރާތަކާއި، ސްކޫލްދަރިވަރުން ހިމެނޭހެން އަހުލުވެރިކޮށް ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމުގެ ޕްރޮގްރާމްތަކެއް ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓުން 2023 ވަނަ އަހަރު ފެށުމަށް ނިންމައި ސަރުކާރު އިދާރާތަކަށް ދައުވަތު ދިނުން
dv.body:
ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، އެ ސިޔާސަތާއިގުޅޭ މުހިންމު މައްސަލަތަކާއި ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދައުލަތުގެ އިދާރާތަކާއި، ސްކޫލްދަރިވަރުން ހިމެނޭހެން އަހުލުވެރިކޮށް ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރު ކުރުމުގެ ޕްރޮގްރާމްތަކެއް ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓުން 2023 ވަނަ އަހަރު ފެށުމަށް ނިންމައި ސަރުކާރު އިދާރާތަކަށް ދައުވަތު ދިނުން

27 އޮކްޓޯބަރު 2021 ގައި ބޭއްވުނު ރައްޔިތުންގެ މަޖިލީހުގެ ތިންވަނަ ދައުރުގެ 31 ވަނަ ޖަލްސާއިން ފާސްކޮށް ޤާނޫނު އަސާސީގެ 92 ވަނަ މާއްދާގައިވާ ގޮތުގެ މަތިން 14 ނޮވެމްބަރު 2021 ވަނަ ދުވަހު ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ ތަޞްދީޤު ކުރައްވާފައިވާ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފޮރިން ސަރވިސްގެ ޤާނޫނަށް މިހާރު ޢަމަލު ކުރަން ފަށާފައިވާތީ، މިނިސްޓްރީގެ ދަށުން ހިންގަމުން އައި ފޮރިން ސަރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓް (ފޮސިމް)ގެ އެންމެހާ މަސައްކަތްތައް ޤާނޫނުގެ ދަށުން ބާރުލިބިގެން ކުރިއަށްގެންދެވޭ އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓަކަށް މިހާރުމިވަނީ ބަދަލު ވެފައެވެ.

ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް ޤާނޫނުގައިވާ ގޮތުގެ މަތީން، ފޮރިން ސަރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓްގެ ޒިންމާތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާގުޅޭ މުހިންމު މައްސަލަތަކާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދައުލަތުގެ އިދާރާތަކާއި، ޢާންމުންނާއި، ކިޔަވާކުދިން އަހުލުވެރިކޮށް، ހޭލުންތެރިކަން އިތުރުކުރުމަކީ ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓުގެ މަސައްކަތްތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން ހިމެނިގެންވާ ކަމެކެވެ.

މިގޮތުން މި އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓް އިން ކުރިއަށް ގެންދާ ފޮސިމް އައުޓްރީޗް ޕްރޮގްރާމުގެ ދަށުން، ސަރުކާރު ވުޒާރާތަކާއި، ސްކޫލް، އަދި ޔުނިވާރސިޓީތަކުގެ ދަރިވަރުންނަށް އަމާޒުކޮށްގެން ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި ގުޅޭ ހާއްސަކަންތައްތަކާއި، މި ސިޔާސަތުގެދަށުން ކުރެވެމުންދާ މަސައްކަތްތަކާ ބެހޭ މަޢުލޫމާތު ދިނުމަށް ތަފާތު އެކި މޮޑިއުލް ތަކަކަށް ބަހާލައިގެން ޕްރޮގްރާމްތަކެއް 2023 ވަނަ އަހަރުން ފެށިގެން ހިންގުމުގެ ތައްޔާރީތައް ފޮރިން ސާރވިސް އިންސްޓިޓިއުޓުން ކުރިއަށް ގެންދަންވަނީ ނިންމާފައެވެ. އަދި މި ސެޝަންތަކުގައި ބައިވެރިވުމުގެ ދައުވަތު ވާނީ، މިހާރު ސަރުކާރު ވުޒާރާތަކާއި، ގައުމީ ޔުނިވާރސިޓީ، ދެވިފައެވެ. އައުޓްރީޗް ޕްރޮގްރާމްގައި ހިންގޭ ސެޝަންތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި، ރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި، ބައިލެޓެރަލް އަދި މަލްޓިލެޓެރަލް ގުޅުންތަކާއި، ކޮމާރޝަލް ޑިޕްލޮމަސީ، ކޮންސިއުލަރ އަދި ޕްރޮޓޮކޯލްތަކާ ބެހޭގޮތުން މައުލޫމާތު ހިއްސާކުރުމުގެ ސެޝަންތައް ކުރިއަށް ދާނެއެވެ.

en.title: Maldives welcomes decision by China to ease travel restrictions in January 2023
en.description: Maldives welcomes decision by China to ease travel restrictions in January 2023
en.body:
Maldives welcomes decision by China to ease travel restrictions in January 2023

The Government of the Republic of Maldives welcomes the announcement by the Government of the People’s Republic of China to end the Covid-19 restrictions for travellers starting from 8 January 2023.

The Government of China will re-open the country to those with work and study visas, or seeking to visit family, and will no longer implement quarantine measures. However, travellers going to China will require a negative test result within 48 hours of departure.

The Maldives looks forward to the resumption of flights between the two countries in the near future, and is eagerly awaiting to welcome back Chinese tourists to the Maldives.

China has been an important contributor to the Maldives’ tourism industry. Prior to the pandemic and the closing of Chinese borders, Chinese travelers to the Maldives numbered over 280,000 arrivals in 2019.

en.title: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel concludes Official Visit to Georgia
en.description: State Minister Ahmed Khaleel concludes Official Visit to Georgia
en.body:
State Minister Ahmed Khaleel concludes Official Visit to Georgia

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel has concluded his Official Visit to Georgia today. State Minister Khaleel undertook this visit to co-chair the second round of political consultations between Maldives and Georgia. Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Georgia, Alexander Khvtisiashvili, co-chaired the consultations on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia.

During the consultations, both State Minister Khaleel and Deputy Minister Khvtisiashvili reviewed the existing relationship between the two countries and explored avenues to further enhance cooperation especially in the fields of trade, tourism, health, education, environment and climate change. The discussions also focused on strengthening economic cooperation including increasing connectivity between the two countries.

During this visit, State Minister Khaleel also met with the Deputy Minister of Economy and Sustainable Development of Georgia, Genadi Arveladze and explored ways to boost trade between the two countries especially in the areas of tourism, fisheries and investment. State Minister Khaleel also met with the Chairperson of the Foreign Relations Committee at the Parliament of Georgia, Nikoloz Samkharadze, and discussed areas to enhance bilateral and multilateral cooperation, including strengthening inter-parliamentary cooperation between the two countries. State Minister Khaleel also met with Maldivian students studying medicine in the Georgian National University SEU in Tbilisi.

State Minister Khaleel was accompanied by Joint Secretary Shiuneen, Rasheed and Desk Officer, Saifulla Waleed during this visit.

Maldives and Georgia hold the 2nd Round of Political Consultation

The second round of political consultations between the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia has concluded in Tbilisi today. The Political Consultation provides a platform between the two countries to discuss bilateral, regional and multilateral issues of mutual importance. The first round of Political Consultation was held in the Maldives on 11 December 2019.   During today’s dialogue, both the governments explored ways to further expand bilateral relations and enhance cooperation in several areas including trade, tourism, health, education, environment and climate change. The discussions also focused on enhancing economic cooperation including increasing connectivity and boosting trade between both the countries. The two governments also discussed international issues of mutual importance and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthen cooperation in the multilateral arena.   The second round of political consultation was co-chaired by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Ahmed Khaleel and the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of Georgia, Alexander Khvtisiashvili.

Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid attends ceremony for the relocation of the Seawall Tetrapod Monument

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today attended a ceremony that was held in Male’ for the relocation of the Seawall Tetrapod Monument. Minister Shahid, together with the visiting State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan, Takei Shunsuke, and the Minister of National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure, Mohamed Aslam, unveiled the Plaque on the monument, which is a token of friendship and cooperation between Maldives and Japan.

Speaking at the ceremony, Minister Shahid expressed his gratitude to the Government of Japan for the Seawall, which had continued to protect the Capital City of Male’ from storm surges and extreme weather events. Minister Shahid also emphasized the importance of the seawall in preventing majore damage to Male’ during the Indian Ocean Tsunami of 2004.

The ceremony was also attended by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives, Takeuchi Midori, Senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of National Planning, Housing and Infrastructure and the Embassy of Japan in the Maldives.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid attends Japan Reception as Guest of Honour
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid attends Japan Reception as Guest of Honour
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid attends Japan Reception as Guest of Honour

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid today attended as the Guest of Honour at the Lunch Reception hosted by the Ambassador of Japan to Celebrate the Official Visit of His Excellency Takei Shunsuke, State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and to commemorate the 55th Anniversary of establishment of diplomatic relations between Maldives and Japan

Speaking at the reception, Minister Shahid extended sincere congratulations on behalf of President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, the Government, and people of Maldives to His Majesty Emperor Naruhito, Emperor of Japan, His Excellency Kishida Fumio, the Prime Minister, and to the friendly people of Japan on the auspicious occasion of the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of Diplomatic relations between Maldives and Japan.

During his remarks while highlighting the historic and friendly nature of the relationship between the two countries, Minister Shahid emphasized the significant advancements achieved in the bilateral relationship between Maldives and Japan, noting the instrumental and constructive role played by the Government towards the development journey of Maldives.

In closing, Minister Shahid thanked Foreign Minister of Japan, Hayashi Yoshimasa for his unwavering determination and commitment to strengthen the relations between our two countries, and thanked Ambassador Midori, for her tireless efforts in elevating the level of cooperation between the Maldives and Japan.

Minister Shahid was joined by State Minister Ahmed Khlaeel, Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef and Ambassador at Large Ahmed Saleem and Senior Officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs at the reception.

en.title: State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the Member of the House of Representatives pays courtesy call on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the Member of the House of Representatives pays courtesy call on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the Member of the House of Representatives pays courtesy call on Foreign Minister Shahid

State Minister of Foreign Affairs of Japan and the Member of the House of Representatives, Takei Shunsuke, paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, today.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid welcomed State Minister Takei Shunsuke to the Foreign Ministry, and highlighted the enduring strength of the Maldives-Japan ties and the close people-to-people contact that form the foundation of the bilateral relationship.

Minister Shahid and State Minister Shunsuke reflected on the close historical relationship between Maldives and Japan, and exchanged views on key areas of bilateral and multilateral interest. In commemoration of the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries, both Minister Shahid and State Minister Takei Shunsuke reaffirmed their commitment to further enhance the partnership bilaterally, within the bilateral and multilateral frameworks.

Minister of State for Foreign Affairs of Maldves, Ahmed Khaleel, Foreign Secretary, Ahmed Latheef, Additional Secretary, Amin Javed Faizal, Senior Undersecretary, Fathimath Naeema and Assistant Director Mohamed Shujau of the Ministry, participated in the meeting.

en.title: State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of the House of Representatives concludes Official Visit to the Maldives
en.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of the House of Representatives concludes Official Visit to the Maldives
en.body:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of the House of Representatives concludes Official Visit to the Maldives

State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of the House of Representatives, Takei Shunsuke has concluded his Official Visit to the Maldives.

State Minister Takei paid courtesy calls on the President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Aminath Shauna, and the Minister of Defence, Uza. Mariya Ahmed Didi. He also signed an Exchange of Notes between the two countries relating to a project on waste management, and attended the ceremony to unveil the Seawall Tetrapod Monument.

Discussions were held between the two sides on an extensive number of issues of common interest, signifying the close nature of the bilateral relationship between Maldives and Japan.

This visit is taking place during the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties between Maldives and Japan. Maldives and Japan established diplomatic relations on 14 November 1967.

State Minister Takei was seen-off at the Velana International Airport by Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Amin Javed Faizal.

en.title: WHO Regional Director for Southeast Asia calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.description: WHO Regional Director for Southeast Asia calls on Foreign Minister Shahid
en.body:
WHO Regional Director for Southeast Asia calls on Foreign Minister Shahid

The Regional Director of the World Health Organization (WHO) for Southeast Asia, Dr. Poonam Khetrapal Singh paid a courtesy call on Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, today. Dr. Khetrapal Singh is currently undertaking an official visit to the Maldives from 18-20 December 2022 upon the invitation of Minister of Health Ahmed Naseem.

During the meeting, Dr. Khetrapal Singh praised the efforts of the Government of Maldives for its response to and recovery efforts to the COVID-19 pandemic. Noting the great strides, the Government has made in the health sector, she commended the Maldives for successfully eliminating many diseases targeted for elimination, including Malaria, Polio and mother-to-child transmission of HIV and syphilis.

Foreign Minister Shahid thanked Dr. Khetrapal Singh for her outstanding leadership and efforts to advance regional health, accelerating the process of immunization and promoting integrated health services. He expressed appreciation for the WHO for prioritizing the need of small states in times of need, especially during the COVID-19 pandemic, by improving health security and resilience.

Foreign Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, Joint Secretary Khadeeja Najeeha, and Chief General Service Officer Aishath Rifga Mohamed.

en.title: State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of House of Representatives arrives in the Maldives on an Official Visit
en.description: State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of House of Representatives arrives in the Maldives on an Official Visit
en.body:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of House of Representatives arrives in the Maldives on an Official Visit

State Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan and Member of House of Representatives His Excellency Takei Shunsuke has arrived in the Maldives today, on an Official Visit to commemorate the 55th Anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Maldives and Japan.

During this visit, State Minister Takei Shunsuke will pay courtesy calls on the President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih, Minister of Foreign Affairs Abdulla Shahid, Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Technology Aminath Shauna, and Minister of Defence, Uza. Mariya Ahmed Didi.

State Minister Takei Shunsuke will also be signing the Exchange of Notes for the grant assistance of 700 million Japanese Yen to be provided by the Government of Japan to enhance sustainable waste management capabilities in the Maldives, and will take part in the unveiling ceremony of the relocation of the Seawall Monument, which was first unveiled in 1990.

State Minister Takei Shunsuke was received by Mr. Amin Javed Faizal, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives.

en.title: Japan to provide 700 million Japanese Yen for Waste Management Project
en.description: Japan to provide 700 million Japanese Yen for Waste Management Project
en.body:
Japan to provide 700 million Japanese Yen for Waste Management Project

The governments of Maldives and Japan today signed Exchange of Notes that will enable the Japanese Government to provide a grant aid of 700 million Japanese Yen (Approximately USD 5.1 million) to the Maldives, to implement a project relating to enhancing the Maldives’ waste management capabilities.

The Exchange of Notes were signed on behalf of the Maldives by Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Ahmed Khaleel, and on behalf of Japan, by the State Minister for Foreign Affairs and Member of House of Representatives, Takei Shunsuke. The ceremony was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Maldives.

This grant aid will be utilised to enhance sustainable waste management capabilities in the Maldives. This includes the provision of waste management equipment, including vehicles for the islands.

While speaking at the ceremony State Minister Khaleel highlighted the generosity of Japanese Government, and thanked the Government of Japan for the grant aid and emphasised the close and friendly relations that exists between the two countries. He further mentioned that such projects reflect Japan’s continued role as one of the key partners in the Maldives’ development journey.

The signing ceremony was attended by the Minister of State for Environment, Climate Change and Technology Khadeeja Naseem, the Ambassador of Japan to the Maldives Takeuchi Midori, and senior officials from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Environment, Climate Change and Technology and Ministry of Finance, as well as the Embassy of Japan.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with the Deputy Chairperson of the Council of Ministers and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dr. Bisera Turković
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with the Deputy Chairperson of the Council of Ministers and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dr. Bisera
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets with the Deputy Chairperson of the Council of Ministers and the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dr. Bisera

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid, met with the Deputy Chairperson of the Council of Ministers and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dr. Bisera Turković, this afternoon.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid welcomed Minister Turković to the Maldives and reviewed the existing bilateral relations between the two countries. Both the Ministers further explored avenues to enhance cooperation between the two countries especially in the areas of trade, education and tourism. Minister Shahid and Minister Turković also reiterated their commitment to intensify the engagement between the two countries in the multilateral spectrum.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by Joint Secretary Shiuneen Rasheed, Assistant Director Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim and Desk Officer Aminath Shaistha Hamdhan Zaki.

Minister Turković’s visit to the Maldives marks the highest-level visit from Bosnia and Herzegovina to the Maldives since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries on 27 January 1997. Minister Turković also made a courtesy call on President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih earlier today.

Let me also take this opportunity to extend my best wishes to Your Excellency’s well-being, success, and for the continued peace, progress and prosperity of the people of Qatar.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to Bhutan

en.title: Ambassador of Maldives to the European Union, Omar Abdul Razzak presents the Letter of Credence to the President of the European Council, Charles Michel
en.description: Ambassador of Maldives to the European Union, Omar Abdul Razzak presents the Letter of Credence to the President of the European Council, Charles Michel
en.body:
Ambassador of Maldives to the European Union, Omar Abdul Razzak presents the Letter of Credence to the President of the European Council, Charles Michel

The newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Maldives to the European Union, Omar Abdul Razzak, presented his Letter of Credence to the President of the European Council, Charles Michel, on 16 December 2022. The ceremony was held at the Headquarters of the General Secretariat of the Council.

During the meeting that followed, President Charles Michel welcomed Ambassador Omar and congratulated him on his appointment. Ambassador Omar conveyed warm greetings and good wishes from the Maldivian people and President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih.

Both Ambassador Omar and President Michel re-affirmed the positive and growing momentum in the Maldives-EU relations over the recent years and re-confirmed their strong interest in further strengthening the excellent bilateral cooperation.

Ambassador Omar was accompanied by Counsellor Ms. Mariyam Seena and First Secretary Ms. Fathimath Reena.

en.title: Ambassador of Maldives to Belgium H.E. Omar Abdul Razzak presents the Letter of Credence to His Majesty King Willem-Alexander of The Netherlands

en.body:
Ambassador of Maldives to Belgium H.E. Omar Abdul Razzak presents the Letter of Credence to His Majesty King Willem-Alexander of The Netherlands

The newly appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Maldives to the Kingdom of the Netherlands, His Excellency Omar Abdul Razzak, presented his Letter of Credence to the King of the Netherlands, His Majesty King Willem-Alexander. The ceremony took place on 14th December 2022, at the Noordeinde Palace in Den Haag.

His Majesty welcomed Ambassador Omar, expressing pleasure to receive the new Ambassador of the Republic of Maldives to the Kingdom of the Netherlands. Ambassador Omar thanked His Majesty the King for the audience and conveyed greetings and good wishes from His Excellency President Ibrahim Mohamed Solih and the people of Maldives.

During the private audience following the Credential Ceremony, Ambassador Omar assured King Willem-Alexander of his commitment to foster closer ties between the two countries and further enhance bilateral cooperation on areas of common interest.

en.title: Foreign Secretary delivers remarks at the Human Rights Day Event organised by UN Maldives and Human Rights Commission
en.description: Foreign Secretary delivers remarks at the Human Rights Day Event organised by UN Maldives and Human Rights Commission
en.body:
Foreign Secretary delivers remarks at the Human Rights Day Event organised by UN Maldives and Human Rights Commission

Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef took part in an event co-hosted by the United Nations Resident Coordinator’s Office and the Human Rights Commission, to mark Human Rights Day 2022. The event held at the Maldives National University today, also commemorated the 75th Anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) under the theme “Dignity, Freedom and Justice for All.”

Delivering Opening Remarks at the event, Foreign Secretary Latheef reaffirmed the commitment of the Maldives to the values of human rights, democracy, and the rule of law. He further recalled the progress achieved by the Maldives in the field of human rights over the years, both domestically and internationally. In this regard, Foreign Secretary Latheef highlighted the efforts undertaken by the Government in enhancing the political and legislative framework to further promote the rights of vulnerable groups, including that of women and children.

Foreign Secretary Latheef also noted the historic election of the Maldives to the membership of the United Nations Human Rights Council for a third time. He expressed hope that assuming a seat at the Council next year would enable the Maldives to continue its advocacy on priority areas such as the intersection between human rights and environment, and democratic consolidation. Lastly he recollected the notable engagements of the Maldives within the Human Rights Council in the past and assured that the country will continue to pursue a future with equality at the core, for its people.

The event also witnessed the participation of the President of Human Rights Commission of the Maldives Mariyam Muna, the United Nations Resident Coordinator Catherine Haswell and members of the diplomatic corps., government dignitaries, the civil society, and the academia. It also featured panel discussions and video screenings on three thematic areas: gender discrimination at the workplace, rights of migrant workers and rights of persons with disabilities.

Human Rights Day is observed every year on 10 December, the day UDHR was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in 1948.

en.title: Minister Shahid sends SAARC Charter Day greetings
en.description: Minister Shahid sends SAARC Charter Day greetings
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends SAARC Charter Day greetings

Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations on the auspicious occasion of the Thirty-Eighth SAARC Charter Day.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and best wishes on the occasion of SAARC Charter Day to the Secretary General of SAARC, the SAARC Secretariat, and the people of the South Asia region.

The SAARC Charter was envisioned to provide a durable mechanism to discuss the common concerns facing our region and address the economic aspirations of our region, with a view to fostering mutual trust and confidence among member nations. It is essential that we interact frequently in order to solve the significant challenges we face as a region and collaborate with one another amicably.

The COVID-19 pandemic has affected societies and economies around the globe and is bound to irreversibly transform communities as it continues to unfold, leaving our region with a series of unprecedented challenges. I firmly believe these obstacles could be surmounted if all member states remain dedicated and continue to collaborate closely, preserving a cohesive atmosphere of friendship and collaboration in the true spirit of SAARC.

Since its creation in 1985, the Maldives has been completely committed to SAARC, and we remain dedicated to cooperating with our neighbors to enhance the Association”.

en.title: Foreign Secretary participates in the 15th Bali Democracy Forum
en.description: Foreign Secretary participates in the 15th Bali Democracy Forum
en.body:
Foreign Secretary participates in the 15th Bali Democracy Forum

Foreign Secretary Ahmed Latheef participated in the 15th Bali Democracy Forum today. He participated in the Forum remotely. The Forum was hosted by the Government of Indonesia and held in hybrid format in Bali, Indonesia. The overarching theme for this Forum was “Democracy in a Changing World: Leadership and Solidarity.”

Foreign Secretary Latheef took part in the panel discussion regarding the democratic responses to fair and equitable access for global public goods. Speaking at the Forum, Foreign Secretary Latheef stressed the importance of strengthening leadership, solidarity, and democratic processes to ensure fair and equitable access to global public goods for everyone. He also elaborated on the efforts undertaken by the current administration to grant access to public goods for the whole population, especially in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic. In this regard, he highlighted the launching of the national vaccination program “Covid-19 Dhifaau” for the entire population, which aimed at vaccinating everyone living in the Maldives, regardless of nationality or legal status.

Emphasizing the need to recognize the natural environment and energy resources as public goods, he noted that the Government is consolidating democratic values, such as inclusivity and accountability, to put in place effective responses to climate change. Further, he stated that the Government is introducing innovative technologies in the fisheries and agricultural sectors to ensure greater food security in the Maldives.

Founded in 2008, the Bali Democracy Forum is an annual international forum held in Bali, Indonesia. The Forum aims to encourage dialogue on advancing regional and global cooperation in the areas of peace and democracy. The Forum brings together senior level Government officials and relevant organizations to share valuable best practices and lesson learnt on building democratic societies.

en.title: Ambassador-at-large participates in the 4th Ministerial Meeting of the Archipelagic Island States Forum
en.description: Ambassador-at-large participates in the 4th Ministerial Meeting of the Archipelagic Island States Forum
en.body:
Ambassador-at-large participates in the 4th Ministerial Meeting of the Archipelagic Island States Forum

Ambassador-at-large at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Ahmed Saleem participated in the 4th Ministerial Meeting of the Archipelagic Island States (AIS) Forum. The meeting was hosted by the Government of Indonesia and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) as the development partner.

Speaking at the Ministerial Meeting, Ambassador Saleem emphasized the importance of vast ocean resources for the Archipelagic Island States, such as the Maldives, as well as the importance of preventing ocean pollution. He further noted that since the fisheries industry accounts for a large percentage of the national GDP, stressors to the environment have direct and indirect impacts on the important economic sectors and the overall development of the economy. Furthermore, Ambassador Saleem noted that the outcomes of the recently concluded COP27 has given hope to any archipelagic and island states, with the establishment of the “loss and damage” fund He also highlighted the importance of working together to change economic systems and lifestyles to more sustainable ones, prioritizing adaptation, utilizing the innovative minds and latest technological breakthroughs.

The Archipelagic and Island States (AIS) Forum is a platform that brings together 47 archipelagic and island states to take part in a collective forum addressing challenges of ocean resource usage for sustainable economic growth, climate change resiliency, ocean pollution, emergency management, and the enhancement of sustainable fisheries.

Ambassador Saleem was accompanied by Mr. Mohamed Thahseen, Assistant Director at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Head of Taskforce for Electoral Campaign Bid Committee Expo 2030 Rome
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Head of Taskforce for Electoral Campaign Bid Committee Expo 2030 Rome
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid meets with Head of Taskforce for Electoral Campaign Bid Committee Expo 2030 Rome

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Abdulla Shahid, met with Head of Taskforce for Electoral Campaign Bid Committee Expo 2030 Rome, Dr. Gaetano Castellini Curiel, this afternoon. The meeting was held as part of the ongoing high-level engagements of Representative Curiel who is currently undertaking a visit to the Maldives from 5 to 7 December 2022.

During the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Minister Shahid reaffirmed the importance attached by the Government of Maldives towards the bilateral relations with Italy, as well as the European Union. He also recognized the contributions made by Italy in kickstarting tourism in the Maldives, and explored further avenues to expand the partnership between both countries on bilateral and multilateral fronts. Minister Shahid further reiterated the request to waive the Schengen Visa requirement for Maldivians and to waive the tariff imposed on Maldivian fish exports to the Europe.

Minister Shahid was accompanied by the Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ahmed Khaleel, Joint Secretary Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Assistant Director Mohamed Shaffau Ibrahim and Assistant Director Aishath Rayahyn.

Representative Curiel was accompanied by the Ambassador of the Italy to the Maldives, Rita Giuliana Mannella, and Honorary Consul Representative of Italy in Maldives Giorgia Marazzi. The delegation met with the Minister of Economic Development, Uz. Fayyaz Ismail earlier today and is expected to meet with the Minister of Environment, Climate Change and Technology, Aminath Shauna, and the Minister of Tourism, Dr. Abdulla Mausoom tomorrow.

en.title: Foreign Minister Shahid sends felicitations on Thailand’s National Day and in commemoration of Late King’s Birthday
en.description: Foreign Minister Shahid sends felicitations on Thailand’s National Day and in commemoration of Late King’s Birthday
en.body:
Foreign Minister Shahid sends felicitations on Thailand’s National Day and in commemoration of Late King’s Birthday

en.title: Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Malaysia
en.description: Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Malaysia
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends Congratulatory Message to the New Foreign Minister of Malaysia

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Maldives, His Excellency Abdulla Shahid has sent a congratulatory message to YB Senator Datuk Seri Diraja Dr. Zambry Abdul Kadir on his appointment as the Minister for Foreign Affairs of Malaysia.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

" It is with great pleasure that I extend to Your Excellency my heartfelt congratulations on your appointment as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malaysia.

As close friends and partners, Maldives and Malaysia have been enjoying years of strong bilateral cooperation that have greatly contributed to our expanding partnership. Let me express my desire to work closely with you at bilateral and multilateral levels for the benefit of our two countries and peoples.

I am confident that with Your Excellency as the Foreign Minister, the Maldives-Malaysia partnership will usher in a new era of cooperation across a multitude of sectors, premised on the values of friendship, mutual respect, and understanding.

I look forward to meet with you and exchange views on the ways for us to further enhance our bilateral cooperation and friendship.

May Allah SWT bless you and your beautiful country with peace, prosperity, and happiness.

Please accept, Your Excellency, the assurance of my highest consideration. "

en.title: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to UAE
en.description: Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to UAE
en.body:
Minister Shahid sends National Day greetings to UAE

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid sends a message of felicitations to His Highness Sheikh Abdullah Bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of the United Arab Emirates, on the occasion of the 51st National Day of the United Arab Emirates.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It is my great honour to extend sincere greetings and well wishes to Your Highness, the Government, and the friendly people of the United Arab Emirates on the momentous occasion of the 51st National Day of the United Arab Emirates.

The shared values of the Maldives and the United Arab Emirates based on Islamic solidarity has enabled our two countries to foster excellent relations over the decades. I am confident that the close ties of friendship and collaboration between our two nations would further strengthen in the years to come.

I also take this opportunity to convey my personal good wishes for Your Highness’ good health and well-being, and for the continued advancement and success of the people of the United Arab Emirates.

Please accept, Your Highness, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

Minister Shahid sends Republic Day Greetings to Central African Republic

The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Maldives, Abdulla Shahid has sent a message of felicitations to the Minister of Foreign Affairs and Central Africans Abroad of the Central African Republic, Mohamed Sylvie Valérie Baipo Temon, on the occasion of the Republic Day of the Central African Republic.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It gives me great pleasure to convey warm greetings and sincere good wishes to Your Excellency, the Government, and the people of Central African Republic, on the occasion of your Republic Day.

Let me also convey, Excellency, my personal best wishes for your good health and well-being, and for further progress of the people of the Central African Republic.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”
